A1.justification: Despite the changed title and conference formatting, both PDFs describe the same conformal prediction framework, methods and benchmark suite. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on decision loss, statistical coverage and classifier-quality sensitivity, including Figures 2–4 and Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Bayesian comparisons, coverage by set size, average set sizes and confidence-adaptivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the penalized conformal score, separable probability-to-cost ratio, greedy label ordering and calibration procedures. Replacing 'decision loss' with 'cost function' changes terminology. The Bayesian experiment uses another probability estimator without changing the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet, iNaturalist, Fitzpatrick and cleaned Fitzpatrick using the same three loss settings. The Bayesian and set-size analyses use retained datasets and tasks; they do not introduce different populations or input environments.

E2.justification: Appendix C and Figure 6 add the Base Bayesian comparator on Fitzpatrick. The original Base Conformal comparisons remain, and the Bayesian-score greedy variants apply existing proposed methods rather than introduce another algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation by set-size buckets and true-label softmax confidence, plus a Bayesian experiment using 25 training epochs and 100 posterior samples per instance. The original 50/25/25 evaluation split, alpha of 0.1 and loss definitions remain unchanged. Newly documented training settings for retained classifiers do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the diagnostic evidence: Tables 1 and 11–14 examine coverage within set-size groups, Figures 5 and 8 examine confidence adaptivity, and Table 10 exposes set-size tradeoffs. Appendix C additionally examines performance with Bayesian estimates. The original classifier-quality ablation and lambda sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 changes from coverage boxplots to explicitly labeled standard-deviation bars, and Figure 5 newly reports mean and standard deviation of true-class softmax scores by set size. The existing ten-run, median-of-means reporting remains; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Tables 2–7 are retained in v2 Tables 4–9. Substantial new results concern Bayesian comparisons, conditional coverage, confidence and set sizes. For example, Table 10 reports CIFAR-100 average sizes of 14.6 for Base Conformal, 5.20 for Penalized Conformal, 22.2 for Greedy Coverage and 23.9 for Greedy Max.

T1.justification: The four propositions, optimization formulations and supporting proofs are substantively unchanged. v1 Sections 5.1–5.5 become v2 Appendix A. The added footnote explaining marginal coverage clarifies an existing guarantee rather than introducing a new assumption or result.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the clinical benefit from 'aiding' triage to 'potentially aiding' triage. The central contributions—three methods, retained coverage guarantees and lower decision costs, including the stated 60–75% reductions—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 extends interpretation to confidence adaptivity, coverage across set sizes and correction of biased Bayesian estimates. Table 10 newly acknowledges that greedy methods improve utility at the expense of larger sets. However, Section 4.2's assertion of valid coverage across all set sizes overstates the subgroup results in Table 14.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents per-dataset training epochs, batch size, learning rate and validation fraction, substantially expanding v1's limited classifier details. Appendix C specifies the Bayesian prior, training objective, training settings and posterior sampling. v2 also embeds a repository destination in the introduction, although its reproducibility statement retains placeholders.

R1.justification: Related work expands beyond the original emphasis on decision-focused learning and conformal prediction to Bayesian neural networks, ensembles, quantile regression and contextual robust optimization. Added discussions and citations include MacKay, Lakshminarayanan, Koenker, Chenreddy, Patel and Yeh, substantially broadening the research context.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, systematically substitutes 'cost function' for 'decision loss', edits introductory explanations and adds thematic related-work headings. It organizes supplementary material into Appendices A–D and adds acknowledgments, while retaining most core exposition and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The conference format substantially changes typography and layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, the full original Figure 3 is relocated as Figure 7, and a compact dermatology comparison becomes the new Figure 3. Bayesian and adaptivity plots, training details and numerous set-size tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and adds useful diagnostics absent from v1, but introduces material interpretation and display problems. Its claim of valid coverage across all set sizes overstates Table 14, which reports 0.71 for Greedy Coverage at sizes 2–4 against a 0.9 target. Figure 3's purported separable-loss panel also shows Fitzpatrick base loss near 6, unexplained against 86.373 in retained Table 4. These benefits and reliability problems prevent a clear net quality judgment.
